source.title: Do VLMs Have Bad Eyes? Diagnosing Compositional Failures via Mechanistic Interpretability
source.authors: Ashwath Vaithinathan Aravindan; Abha Jha; M. Kulkarni

record.file_problem: None; full paper text supplied, with some equations and tables flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures neuron-level feature entanglement in a vision encoder, extending neuron-superposition analysis to a visual model. It does not test any listed version's specific audit, model scope, explanation-fidelity, or scoring claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports neuron feature affinities and a relationship between superposition and embedding-space measures; these are recorded below as findings about the claim's broader subject, with versions ["none"]. The Grad-CAM prompt examples concern visual grounding rather than the specified neuron claims and are not included as rows. The paper gives no share of neurons with one or two jobs and does not test explanations on held-out activations.
record.test_reason: The study measures multi-feature responses of selected MLP neurons in CLIP-ViT-L/14 on a toy shapes dataset, and links them to embedding separability. It tests none of the versions. It has no Qwen3 or language-model audit and no share of one-job, two-job or unexplained neurons (V1, V2). It does not reanalyse canonical polysemantic neurons or pose (V3). It has no architecture, regularization or tool comparison (V4), no attribution graphs (V5), and no held-out prediction or simulation scoring of explanations (V6, V7). The record's own tranche reason says as much, so 'tests/T3' is inconsistent. The results belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it understates the authors' framing. They conclude that superposition exists down to individual CLIP neurons, many of which 'may encode multiple, semantically unrelated attributes'. They call it 'a key bottleneck' for compositionality, and the abstract says it 'directly hinders' it. The weak-correlation caveat and the call for causal follow-up appear in the results and limitations, not the conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a toy visual dataset, top-activating images, feature-affinity entropy, and embedding-space measures. It does not use neuron-pole audits or explanation-prediction tests.

fits_no_version.finding: In CLIP-ViT-L/14, selected low-entropy MLP output neurons have affinities to several shape, colour and position features on a 500-image toy dataset. Pairwise superposition S is weakly associated with smaller embedding centroid distance and higher nearest-centroid misclassification.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a CLIP vision encoder, some MLP neurons respond to several simple visual attributes, and pairwise feature overlap across neurons is weakly associated with poorer embedding separability of those attributes.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
record.problems: Evidence is limited to one model and a small synthetic toy dataset. The authors describe the relationship between superposition and compositional performance as weak, note that the study does not establish a direct causal link, and state that high-entropy neurons may have preferred features underrepresented or absent from the dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant neuron results left out. Grad-CAM examples in Section 4.2 were excluded because they report spatial grounding behavior, not the neuron properties or explanation tests named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, no neuron poles, no one-job/two-job/unexplained shares.
No language models, dense or MoE, and no scale sweep. The study covers one vision encoder only.

No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive-generalization analysis. The multi-feature CLIP neurons are interpreted as superposition, but no test separates that from a coherent shared feature.
No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools, and no interpretable-neuron share estimates.
No attribution graphs or circuit sufficiency test.
No explanations tested on held-out activations (Figure 4 is a qualitative check on a few images of one neuron).
No simulation-based scoring of automated explanations.

missing.what: Entropy distribution of all 24,576 MLP output neurons on the toy dataset. It is the only population-level view, with high-entropy neurons said to show no clear pattern. No numeric shares are given.
Patch-wise activation maps of neuron 16/563 on test images: strong activation on circles, squares, pink and red, and low activation on a triangle-only image.

record.verdict_notes: Workshop paper (ICCVW 2025). Affinity values in the tables (e.g. 0.57, 0.57, 0.53) do not sum to 1 as the stated formula requires; the text also describes them as average activation when the feature is present, so the metric is ambiguous. Superposition is inferred from top-30 co-occurrence in multi-object images, with no control for attribute co-occurrence. The chosen 'feature neurons' are the most selective, so they say nothing about what share of neurons are clean. The Grad-CAM section on binding failures is correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B, distinguish positive and negative neuron poles, or estimate the stated one-job, two-job, and not-understood shares.
Studies one vision encoder, not other language models or dense and mixture-of-experts language models; no scale sweep or share estimates.
Does not study InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not compare architectures, regularization, or tools, or estimate interpretable-neuron shares for InceptionV1-sized models.
Does not construct attribution graphs or test whether neurons suffice as circuit units.
Does not produce neuron explanations and test their predictions on activations not used to write them.
Does not score automated neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Ranked neuron activations over toy-dataset images and reported feature affinities and entropy for selected neurons.
rows.value: Entropy 3.36 (0.18 %ile); top features: Circle (0.57), Pink (0.57), Square (0.53), Top-Left (0.4), Red (0.3).
rows.note: The paper describes the neuron as activating for multiple visual features.
rows.check: Hand-picked low-entropy neuron, a selection value rather than a population estimate, so it cannot bear on shares of clean neurons. Entropy 3.36 against a maximum of log2(16)=4 is fairly spread. Images hold 1–5 objects, so co-occurring features in top images can inflate apparent multi-feature affinity. 'Observed' has no version to be observed against.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Compared the superposition measure for feature pairs with their embedding cluster-center distance, using the 1000 lowest-entropy neurons.

conditions.value: superposition S versus cluster-center distance D

rows.measure: Relationship between superposition and cluster-center distance
rows.value: Feature pairs with higher S have smaller D; the paper describes the correlation as weak.
rows.note: The paper reports a directional relationship but no numeric correlation value.

rows.subject: CLIP-ViT-L/14
rows.operation_detail: Compared the superposition measure for feature pairs with embedding misclassification rate, using the 1000 lowest-entropy neurons.

conditions.value: superposition S versus misclassification rate M

rows.measure: Relationship between superposition and misclassification rate
rows.value: Feature pairs with higher S have higher M; the paper describes the overall connection between superposition and compositional reasoning as weak and warranting further investigation.
rows.note: The paper reports a directional relationship but no numeric correlation value.
